page: Hetzner Cloud cx33 is an x86_64 virtual server based on the QEMU hypervisor. It features 4 shared vCPUs powered by AMD EPYC processors running at 2.0 GHz, with 4 physical cores and 1.0 thread per core. The system is equipped with 8.0 GB of RAM, yielding 1.95 GB of memory per core, and includes 80 GB of local SSD storage. It does not include any complimentary public IPv4 addresses or dedicated GPU hardware.

Performance benchmarks show strong single-core CPU capabilities, with stress-ng single-core performance scoring 2672.38, placing it in the top 25%. Multi-core performance is average, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 10641.52 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 4852.0. Memory performance is a bottleneck, as the Passmark memory score of 1766.43 falls into the bottom 25%, despite average memory bandwidth speeds of 470.59 GB/sec for cached small blocks. Other areas of weakness include software compilation with Clang and static web serving throughput, both ranking in the bottom 25%.

Given its shared CPU allocation and lower memory-to-vCPU ratio, the cx33 is a budget-friendly option for workloads with moderate resource demands. It is suited for basic database operations, scoring an average 3447.6 on Passmark database tests, and Redis deployments, which achieved 7.84 million SET operations per second. It can also support small-scale language model inference, processing 179.98 tokens per second for text generation on a 135M parameter model, though it is constrained on larger models.
